answer.question: What should an Oakleaf turf plan keep from the existing landscape?
answer.answer: Confirm the parcel’s Branan Field Corridor requirements and retain any required planting; synthetic turf cannot simply replace those plants. Identify protected trees and resolve any necessary tree-preservation review before preparation affects roots. Bring community requirements and the property plan to the estimate.

paras: Start with the path from the door and the spots your dog uses most. A dedicated area can leave room for a patio, planting or a compact green. Include a water source and access for waste pickup and cleaning.
If the yard stays wet, show us rain photos and existing drains. The cause of a water or odor problem needs to be considered separately from replacing the visible surface.

blocks.h2: Leave the required landscape in place.
paras: The Branan Field Corridor has residential landscape and tree requirements. Check the applicable boundary and conditions for your parcel; required planting does not become optional when a turf area is added. Work affecting protected trees can need an approved preservation plan.

Obtain the current instructions from the appropriate neighborhood association and check any CDD or shared-area conditions. The Oakleaf commercial area across the Duval line has a different jurisdiction, so use the exact work address rather than the area name alone.

blocks.h2: Boulogne sand holds water a foot below your yard.
paras: A USDA soil query along Oakleaf Plantation Parkway returns Boulogne fine sand: poorly drained, with the water table about a foot down at its highest and a hydrologic rating of C/D, meaning water soaks in slowly (USDA). Its first organic-stained layer can start just 10 to 13 inches below the surface. Rain here doesn't vanish into the sand the way people expect in Florida.

Along Double Branch Creek and its tributaries the survey adds Pamlico muck and Rutlege mucky fine sand, with pockets of Yulee clay in the low spots. Put that under a small fenced yard the dog uses every day and you get the familiar Oakleaf complaint: mud after every afternoon storm, and grass the dog finishes off.

So the base is built for drainage rather than laid on grade: the right excavation depth, drainage aggregate and, where the yard needs it, a subsurface drain tied out. We test the ground when we come out for the free visit, then design the base for your lot. The county's code names the same risk: Sec. 18.5-53(4)(g) calls for solid sod in swales and other areas subject to erosion.

blocks.h2: Here, Clay County's landscaping code follows you home.
paras: Oakleaf Plantation sits inside the Branan Field Corridor, which Sec. 18.5-52(22) draws from the Duval line along Little Black Creek, Black Creek and North Fork Black Creek to the eastern edge of Jennings State Forest. Inside it, Sec. 18.5-51 applies the county's landscaping article to residential buildings as well as businesses, and Sec. 18.5-53(4)(h) bars artificial turf as a substitute for the plants the article requires (Clay County code). Where your lot carries required plantings, keep them, and put the turf around them.

Trees matter most on a turf job. Within the corridor, Secs. 18.5-27 to 18.5-32 make it unlawful to cut, remove, damage, root-disturb or even trim a protected tree without an approved tree preservation plan, and trenching a base edge beside a street tree is exactly that kind of work. Along rights-of-way the corridor also asks for a wider landscaped yard, 10 feet instead of 5. Check your parcel against the corridor's boundary before anything is designed.

Above the county sit two community development districts, Double Branch and Middle Village, and under them each neighbourhood's POA with its own architectural review (Double Branch CDD). Oakleaf Town Center, meanwhile, lies across the line in Jacksonville, so commercial work there follows Duval's code, not Clay's.

blocks.h2: Irrigation once a week, and fines that count by the day.
paras: Oakleaf's water comes from Clay County Utility Authority. The district's Phase III Order 2026-017 was in force at our 7 September 2026 check, and it cuts lawn irrigation to a single weekly day, set by your address, from every source including private wells (Clay County Utility Authority).
The county writes the schedule into its own code at Sec. 18.5-73 and enforces it under Sec. 18.5-79, where every day of watering on the wrong day counts as a new offense.
CCUA runs a reclaimed water program, so ask whether your phase is on it, but it offers no rebate for artificial turf (CCUA). The case for turf in Oakleaf is the mud and the dog, not the water bill.

faq.q: Who installs artificial turf in Oakleaf Plantation, FL?
faq.a: We install pet turf, artificial lawns and backyard putting greens in Oakleaf Plantation, FL. Oakleaf asks two things of a turf job: a base for Boulogne fine sand, which drains poorly and holds its water table about a foot down, and a layout that respects Clay County's Branan Field Corridor, where the county's landscaping and tree rules reach homes. Call 303-349-2368 for a free estimate.

faq.q: Is my Oakleaf home inside the Branan Field Corridor?
faq.a: Oakleaf Plantation sits inside it: the corridor reaches west to Jennings State Forest, which Eagle Landing borders. Check your own parcel against the boundary in Sec. 18.5-52(22) before you plan the yard (Clay County code). Inside it, the county's landscaping and tree rules apply to homes, not only businesses.

faq.q: Do I need a tree preservation plan to put in turf?
faq.a: Only if the work would cut, damage, root-disturb or trim a protected tree. Within the corridor, Secs. 18.5-27 to 18.5-32 require an approved tree preservation plan before any of that (Clay County code). Keep the base edge clear of protected roots, or get the plan approved first.

faq.q: What happens if I water on the wrong day in Oakleaf?
faq.a: A first violation is a category 2 civil infraction under Sec. 18.5-79, and later ones are category 10, up to $500 if you contest and lose (Clay County code). Each day is a separate offense, and the county gives no more than one written warning.

faq.q: Does my CDD or POA have to approve turf?
faq.a: Your neighbourhood POA's architectural review does, and the two CDDs, Double Branch and Middle Village, set the rules for the amenities they run (Middle Village CDD). Send the POA the layout you approve with us before any work starts.
